# Session Log — 2026-09

Append-only. Newest entry at the bottom. One entry per session, written by
the chronicler BEFORE the session's final commit so the entry rides in it.
Format: `## <date> — <issue/trigger> — <outcome>`, then what was
attempted/shipped (commit hash), ratchet movement, decisions, surprises,
friction, next.

`Spec: n/a` is not an omission but the oracle's finding, since STYLE P3 gives a marker an area tag *"never a rule ID or clause"* and all five spec files return **zero matches for "GAP"**; the arbiter **REJECTED** round 1 on two blocking findings that are both *measurement-instrument* defects rather than judgment errors about ownership — a citation placed after the marker's bullet list, which `tools/gapaudit`'s `paragraph()` never reaches, and a no-owner rewrite naming OPEN #499/#578 while disclaiming them, which its bare `#(\d+)` `citations` scan cannot tell from an ownership claim — each moving the audit the wrong way in **opposite** directions, so the repair's totals are **unchanged at census 66 / group 1 17 / group 2 25** and the **four-row membership diff is the whole measurement**; the arbiter agreed with all three NO OWNER rulings, with the deletion, and raised no finding against any of the ten repoints, and it found the two defects only by taking the reconciliation measurement mason had skipped *"for want of an issue list on stdin"* in a container where docs/ROUTINES.md's **Survey input** recipe works; **`Ratchet: unchanged`** run rather than inferred, `surface: unchanged`, 8 files **+31/−32**, all `.go`, and `git diff origin/main...HEAD -U0` filtered to anything not starting `//` is **empty across both commits** — not one executable line moved.

- Surprises:
  - **Both blocking defects are invisible to a prose read and visible only to
    the instrument.** `bulletPattern` and a blank comment line are hard
    paragraph boundaries in `tools/gapaudit`, whose `marker` type states the
    contract outright — *"[paragraph]'s boundary rules decide what counts as
    cited"* — so a citation placed after a marker's bullets is not in the
    marker's text at all; and `citations` is a bare `#(\d+)` scan whose own
    doc says there is *"no signal here to tell the two apart"*. The first left
    `validate/cvcelt.go:154` in group 1 with **#1119 still in group 2**, the
    exact pathology the issue exists to fix; the second did the reverse,
    silencing a correct group-1 row so a gap this landing rules unowned read
    as tracked, and pulling **#499 out of group 2** while #499's real marker
    stayed in group 1.
  - **The repair moves no total.** Census 66, group 1 17, group 2 25 before
    and after, because the two findings move in opposite directions and
    cancel. A totals-only check would have shown a clean repair as a no-op and
    the rejected commit as equally good; the membership diff — exactly four
    rows, and nothing else — is the only reading that distinguishes them.
  - **A fifteenth site carries finding 1's exact mechanism and is pre-existing
    on `main`.** Found by mason's own grep for surviving copies of the claim
    it was correcting, not by the audit.
  - **Mason's reason for leaving that fifteenth site was wrong even though the
    call was right.** The account argued that fixing it *"would change the very
    membership this repair round exists to demonstrate"*; the arbiter ruled
    that protecting a baseline is never grounds for leaving a defect, since a
    measurement is an observation of the tree and the tree owes it nothing.
    The sound reasons are that it is pre-existing on `main` and outside a
    repair instruction already written as closed — and that enlarging the ask
    at round 2 under a two-round cap is the failure the cap exists to prevent.
  - **Mason's reflow worry was already closed by #1117.**
    `hashEndsParagraph` returns **false** for a `#` immediately followed by
    digits, so a future `commentwrap` reflow moving `#1119` to a line start
    cannot drop it. The new mid-paragraph host is stable.

**ZERO unblocked and the zero is measured; ZERO issues filed; ONE watch-item
DISMISSED with both arms of its recorded reversal trigger measured cold rather
than assumed, and the trigger SHARPENED into a form the next pass re-tests in
one grep; ONE friction pattern confirmed still unrouted and not duplicated
here.** No issue body needed correcting — this landing falsified no premise
anywhere in the queue, which is what a doc-only change with no exported-surface
delta should do and is written down because a checked-and-empty result and a
skipped check are otherwise indistinguishable from `git log` (#400).

- **Unblock sweep: ZERO, measured.** **No open issue's `## Depends on` names
  #409**, and none of the **20** open `blocked` issues mentions it in one. Feed
  taken from the REST issues endpoint after the merge per docs/ROUTINES.md's
  **Survey input** recipe — 12 pages at `per_page=100`, every page but the last
  full, **1162** items reshaping to **664** non-PR issues of which **252** are
  open. Sixteen open bodies contain the digits `409`; **eleven carry a real

  #1144, #1123, #1003, #896, #748, #671, #670, #625, #513, #492, #472, all
  filing it as *adjacent*, *related-not-gating*, or (in #896's case) *"Not

  … **#409**, the doc.go present-tense contract sweep …)"* and #472's

  cites `+9409`. #409 was filed `Depends on: none` and nothing was ever queued
  behind it. `wip/issue-409` is gone from the remote, as a merged lease should
  be — 10 heads remain.
- **The arbiter's `# Determinism` watch-item: DISMISSED, and the dismissal is
  a measurement, not a judgment call.** The landing entry recorded the item with
  a two-arm reversal trigger; both arms were tested at `c5b789b`.

    '{{len .TestGoFiles}}{{len .XTestGoFiles}}' ./codegen` prints `00`; the
    package is still one file.
  - **Arm 1 (a second present-tense claim under a lead-in) — cold, on a

## 2026-09-01 — #1115 with #441 — **§3.2.1's simple-type-only typing of an Attribute Declaration's `{type definition}` is enforced at construction for the first time, so `ownedTypeFold`'s absence of attribute-side roots stops being a convention and becomes a consequence — the `GAP(xsd)` marker and both paragraphs arguing the unenforced state DELETE, and `gapaudit`'s census reads 66 → 65**: `xsd.NewAttributeDeclaration` now rejects an `InlineTypeDefinition` wrapping a `ComplexType` and charges **`a-props-correct` clause 1**, deliberately not `xsderr.RuleComponentInvariant` — the element side's twin rejection stays `RuleComponentInvariant` because THERE the shape is legal and only the entry point is wrong, and one test table drives both refs through both constructors so the asymmetry is pinned in one place; the oracle's finding is the one that settles the design fork #1115's body left open — **option (b) (widen `ownedTypeFold`'s roots to the attribute side) is not merely costlier than (a), it is spec-FORECLOSED by it**, since §3.4.2.4 clause 3 and §3.4.2.5 clause 2 read `{attribute uses}`/`{attribute wildcard}` and never an attribute declaration's own type slot's variety, so once (a) holds there is nothing complex-shaped at that slot for a widened root to ever reach; the same grounding's queue search found **#441 — open since 2026-08-02, `ready`, `kind/bug`, no live branch — is the identical fix already fully specified, and specified BETTER** (it settles the rule ID and the placement that #1115 leaves implicit), so the two were absorbed into one landing rather than one of them being re-derived; the arbiter **REJECTED** round 1 on one finding and it is a defect of the SWEEP, not of the change — the stale-marker sweep found two of three cross-references and missed the third **in the same package as the deletion**, `ComplexType.AttributeUses`'s doc, which the arbiter found with the one `grep -rn ownedtypefold` the sweep should have run; **`Ratchet: unchanged`** run rather than inferred, lane totals an exact match across both rounds, `surface: unchanged` both rounds, 7 files **+110/−49**.

- Decisions made and why:
  - **`a-props-correct` clause 1, not `xsderr.RuleComponentInvariant`.**
    §3.2.1's tableau types `{type definition}` as a Simple Type Definition
    with no complex arm, and clause 1 is *"the values of the properties … are
    as described in the property tableau"* — so a wrapped `ComplexType` breaks
    a spec clause a CALLER violates, not a representation invariant this
    package owns (STYLE E2). Every other `ruleAPropsCorrect` site in the file
    stands on the same sentence about a different property.
  - **The check lives in `NewAttributeDeclaration`, not behind
    `checkTypeDefinitionOrRef`.** That checker's slot switch decides which ARM
    a slot admits, on this package's representation footing, and charges
    `RuleComponentInvariant` throughout; routing a spec verdict through it
    would make one switch return two rule families. This mirrors
    `NewElementDeclaration`'s existing `ownedComplexType()` rejection, which
    is the pattern #441 prescribed and which is still the live one.
  - **Ordering inside the constructor is deliberate**: `checkTypeDefinitionOrRef`
    runs FIRST, so a wrapped *named* `ComplexType` keeps its `component-invariant`
    charge (arm well-formedness before tableau conformance) and the new guard
    only ever fires on an otherwise well-formed anonymous inline type. Nothing
    pins that combination — the arbiter checked it from the source and ruled it
    **not a finding**, because the behaviour for that input is byte-identical
    to `origin/main`.
  - **The `Direction (STYLE P3a)` paragraph was deleted whole, not preserved.**
    P3a governs a claimed error direction on a GAP; with the gap gone there is
    no direction to substantiate. Its inventory of `ResolvedSimpleType`
    narrowing sites now exists nowhere in the tree — mason flagged exactly that
    as the thing to scrutinise hardest, and the arbiter ruled the loss real but
    not a cost: every site it named is one `grep -rn ResolvedSimpleType` away,
    and the invariant it argued for is enforced by construction now.
  - **Two cross-reference rewrites absorbed** (`parser/produce_complex.go`'s
    `produceComplexType`, `validate/assess.go`'s `walk.unmatchedAttribute`),
    one sentence each, no rule ID outside the grounding, no surface, no lane

- Decisions made and why:
  - **A fourth three-root walk in `xsd`, not a widened `componentWalk`.** The
    issue offered "extend `componentWalk` with a type-table capability, or
    hand-roll the descent"; both were declined for what the shared walk
    ENUMERATES, not what it charges. Entering `{type table}` slots in
    `walkElementDeclaration` would make `checkTypeTableSubstitutability` charge
    e-props-correct clause 7 against declarations nested inside
    alternative-owned types, and `checkComponentValueConstraints` clause 2 the
    same — new verdicts in passes this issue does not own and cannot attribute
    to its own ratchet movement. A `complexType` hook on `componentWalk` would
    charge the `<redefine>` original its `walkComplexType` deliberately enters
    as a component in its own right (#843), which is #584's change. What is
    NOT duplicated is the slot enumeration: `walkElementDeclaration` calls
    `ownedTypeSlots`, the single producer, whose doc now names three readers.
    **The cost is stated rather than hidden — `xsd` now holds four three-root
    walks** (`componentwalk.go` + its two callers, `ownedtypefold.go`,
    `allgrouplimited.go`'s hand-rolled one, and this) — and both mason and the
    arbiter ruled it a **T4 question for the steward, not a correctness one**,
    since `checkAllGroupsLimited` already covers the anonymous shape by its own
    descent.
  - **An owned `{base type definition}` is entered to reach the declarations
    inside it and charged nothing** — the same split
    `ownedTypeFold.ownedBase`/`.ownedTypeSlot` already draws — because the
    body's exclusion of `s.modelGroupRedefinitions` is an exclusion of the
    base-seating mechanism generally. Pinned by
    `TestWalkEntersAnOwnedBaseWithoutChargingIt`'s two subtests.
  - **No visited set, and the soundness argument is the walk's, not an
    inheritance.** Every edge followed is an ownership edge — `ResolvedTerm`
    wraps an already-known `Term` and `<element ref>`/`<group ref>` are never
    rewritten into it, `ownedComplexType` admits only the
    `InlineTypeDefinition` arm — so the structure is a finite tree and
    PRINCIPLES 9 holds without a guard. One anonymous type can still be
    charged more than once (a `{default type definition}` aliasing the
    declaration's own type, a base's particle inside an extension's); each
    pass decides a property of the component alone at a `Loc` the component
    carries, so this is verdict-preserving and costs **~4% of conformance wall
    time** (327s against a 313s pre-change baseline on the same machine).
  - **A THIRD GAP marker, at the root set, beyond the two the verdict named.**
    Mason's judgement call, flagged as one; the arbiter ruled it in scope
    under WORKFLOW's scope rule (no rule ID the grounding lacks, no exported
    surface, cannot move a lane) and kept it, because a gap whose cause is the
    root set belongs where the root set is chosen and the other two markers get
    shorter by pointing at it. **No new issue filed for the residue** — #584's
    title already scopes it as "an ANONYMOUS complex type reached only through
    an owning slot gets no Phase D verdict".
  - **`validate/icfixture_test.go`'s `icAnonymousSchema` was spec-invalid and
    is now an extension.** Its `<kid>` type was an anonymous RESTRICTION of a
    `Base` with no attribute use and no `{attribute wildcard}` while declaring

## 2026-09-02 — #472 — **`goxsd8 parse` is the first subcommand that does work, and the whole summary is built from #252's published accessors and nothing else (`surface: unchanged` at both rounds, which is exactly what sequencing this after #252 bought)**: `parse <schema.xsd>...` compiles each argument and prints its namespaces, a count per §3.17.1 property and a total on stdout, exit 0 when every argument compiles, **1** with the first error on stderr in `(*xsderr.Error).Error()`'s own rendering, and **2** for a usage or IO fault — the split made by **opening the document before `parser.Parse` sees it** rather than by archaeology on the returned error chain, which is what keeps `is a directory` (charged `[xml-wf]` by the parser) out of the verdict bucket; the six decisions the body demanded are stated once in the three copies that must agree (`doc.go`, `main.go`'s `usage` const, `README.md`) — one run per argument in argument order with the exit code the worst outcome, **git-style** positional grammar with a fourth diagnosis so `goxsd8 -q parse a.xsd` stops answering *"no subcommand given"* while every pinned `dispatchCases` row survives, `-q` scoped to informational output and **never** a diagnosis (the rule that binds `validate`'s stdout violation lines from #1066 too), `-help=true` a usage error at every position, and `-version` kept a non-flag; the **`Spec:` line is `n/a` on the oracle's finding, not by omission** — `xmlschema11-1.md` §2.4's own note disclaims the subject outright (*"This specification defines no API or other interface for interacting with schemas"*), so the only spec contact is that the CLI is a **pure conduit** for whatever rule ID the parser already attached; the arbiter **REJECTED** round 1 on eight findings of which **not one was about a design decision** — two of the three tests mason's own account named load-bearing **could not fail**, and the arbiter proved both by mutation rather than by reading, because no fixture had two namespaces (so `namespacesOf`, the diff's only order-producing code, was unpinned and the map-range mutant its own comment names passed the whole package) and the single error fixture returned **unwrapped** (so deleting `violationLine`'s `errors.As` unwrap shipped green, with `parser:` in the contract's location field); *"one line per error on stderr"* was meanwhile **false of shipped behaviour in five places**, `parser/parse.go:146` returning only the first error; the repair delivered all eight, bought a two-namespace `<xs:import>` pair **named so that first-appearance and sorted order disagree** and a malformed-XML document the parser returns wrapped, and filed **#1185** so the `GAP(cmd)` marker earns a tracker in the order `docs/WORKFLOW.md:449` runs it; round 2 **ACCEPTED with no findings** after the arbiter re-ran all four mutations itself — two of them its own — against a 55-run clean baseline; **`Ratchet: unchanged`, measured not assumed** (`go list -deps ./conformance | grep -c cmd/goxsd8` is `0`, so no lane can observe this diff), 11 files **+1032/−91**, nothing exported.

- Cost — **1 oracle, 2 mason (1 repair), 2 arbiter (1 reject).** No warden
  (`surface: unchanged`, confirmed by outcome), no cartographer (**mason filed
  #1185 itself**, as the marker's tracker rather than as planning), no steward.
  **What the reject bought is two dead tests made live and one false contract
  clause retired — not a different answer about the change**: round 1 accepted
  every design decision on the merits, including the one mason asked to have
  scrutinized hardest, and still found that the diff's own account of which tests
  were load-bearing was wrong about two of three.
- Decisions made and why:
  - **Multi-schema is one run per argument, not one combined set.** `parser.Parse`
    takes a single root location, so a combined set needs a library change and is
    out of scope; the runs are independent, errors are **not** deduped, every
    argument is reported however the one before it went, and the exit code is the
    max over 0/1/2 with the constants ordered by severity for that purpose. Beats
    stop-at-first-failure, which hides verdicts one pass could have given.
  - **The exit-2 split is made at the seam, not by classifying an error.** Opening
    the document in `rootLocation` before handing it to `parser.Parse` is what
    produces `goxsd8: parse: open testdata/nosuch.xsd: no such file or directory`
    instead of a three-clause loader chain, and it is what makes
    `TestParseFaultsAreDistinguishable` a property test rather than a shape
    assertion: five kinds, distinct codes, pairwise-distinct stderr. This
    discharges the asymmetry the thread has carried since 2026-08-16 — `validate`'s
    blurb reserved 2 and `parse`'s did not.
  - **Git-style grammar, with the fourth diagnosis rather than a second parse of
    the vocabulary.** `leadingFlagFmt` fires only when a real subcommand follows;
    `noSubcommand` survives for a leading flag with nothing after it, so the
    `-version` and `-help=true` rows stay pinned. Go-style — a leading flag as a
    usage error naming the missing subcommand — would have meant a second
    pre-dispatch parse of the same flag names, which is a second encoding of them
    (D3). Two independent cliuser witnesses had reported the old misdiagnosis, and
    the `/backlog` declined to split it out precisely because the grammar cannot be
    stated until a subcommand parses its own flags; this is that subcommand.
  - **The resolver is rooted at the filesystem root, dropping `loader.Dir`'s
    confinement — accepted on the merits, and the repair added the disclosure.**
    It is the only rooting under which all three hold at once: an absolute or `../`
    argument works, a relative `<xs:include>` resolves against its own document's
    directory, and the `<loc>` an error cites is a path the reader can open (the
    conformance harness's base-name pattern would print `broken.xsd:9:3` for
    `parse a/b/broken.xsd` and fail that bar). `loader/dir.go:19-22` frames the
    confinement as a defence against a location *"treated as an untrusted, possibly
    attacker-supplied hint"* and calls it an engineering decision, not a spec rule;
    a CLI reading documents its own invoking user named, with that user's
    privileges, has no attacker in that position. **The finding was never the
    behaviour — it was that a changed security-relevant default lived only in a
    source comment**, so `doc.go`'s Argument vocabulary now says *"confined to no
    subtree: a schema document may name any path the invoking user can read, so an
    `<xs:include schemaLocation="../../../etc/passwd">` is served like any other"*,
    and the arbiter ruled the concrete consequence better than the sentence it had
    asked for.
  - **The summary reports the namespaces the compiled set's components are in, and
    that is an API finding recorded rather than an export.** `*xsd.Schema` has no
    target-namespace accessor and **§3.17.1 gives the Schema component no `{target
    namespace}` property at all** — it belongs to each schema *document*. The
    residual is honest and stays open: a document with `targetNamespace="X"` that
    declares no global components contributes no namespace line, because nothing
    observable carries X. Reporting a document's declared namespace needs a new
    accessor and a warden pre-flight; nothing was exported.
  - **Each bucket is filtered to components carrying a source position.** `xsd`'s
    package doc is what fixes the zero `Loc` as *"the correct value for a component
    with no schema document behind it"*; unfiltered, every schema reports the same
    54 seeded builtins instead of `order.xsd`'s 2. Flagged by mason for scrutiny
    and ruled sound.
  - **The vacuous `parser:` assertion was MOVED, not duplicated.** The
    `src-resolve` fixture returns unwrapped and can never reach the unwrap branch,
    so leaving a check there that no mutation can fail is the defect the reject
    named. The arbiter confirmed the move cost nothing: under the unwrap mutation
    the full-package run names exactly one `--- FAIL`.
  - **The error-count clause is amended, not defended.** The issue's own Spec
    section granted *"implement it as written, or amend all three copies
    deliberately and in one commit"*; `parser/parse.go:146` is the authority
    (*"Like Produce, ParseReport returns only the first error"*), and the amended
    clause landed in `doc.go`, `usage`, `README.md` and the two further sites the
    verdict had not named — `main_test.go`'s pins and `parse_test.go`'s own doc
    comment. `README.md`'s *one per line* for `validate` is left alone: that is
    `validate`'s unbuilt contract, not a claim about shipped behaviour.
- Surprises:
  - **The reject was entirely about test quality, and the tests it killed are the
    ones mason's own account nominated.** The account's *"the ones that would catch
    a mutation rather than decorate the diff"* list had three entries and two of
    them could not fail. Nothing in the diff's design was wrong; the arbiter said
    so at length and rejected anyway.
  - **A `-count=1` package run is not a mutation test.** The map-range mutant
    survived thirteen tests and a 21-run byte comparison because the fixture had
    one namespace, so `order` never held two elements and map iteration had nothing
    to permute — what the determinism test proved was that the *counts* were
    stable, which no map was ever going to threaten.
  - **Go 1.26's iteration over the repaired two-entry map is not an even coin, and
    the arbiter stated the residual rather than rounding it to "fixed"**:
    `TestParseNamespaceOrder` alone catches the mutant ~15% of the time and the
    21-run comparison ~95%, which is 21 draws at p≈0.135, so roughly one run in
    thirty lets it through the package. **Not a finding** — the committed code is
    deterministic across 55 clean runs and the 21 is the count round 1 itself
    prescribed — but the knob is recorded: the loop count *is* the sensitivity,
    and 20 → 100 takes the escape to ~1e-6.
  - **The fixture pair was named so first-appearance and sorted order disagree**,
    which is why two different mutation classes are covered by two tests that are
    not redundant: `slices.Sort` fails the golden block 3/3, the map range fails
    the determinism loop. The arbiter verified both claims rather than reading them.

    moment `parse` shipped.** Nobody wrote it wrongly; T6 turned three copies of an

- Decisions made and why:
  - **The ancestor question is answered on the XML tree, not on the component
    graph.** Clause 4.3.1/4.3.2 are stated over XML *ancestors*, so a
    `<restriction>` reached through a named `<group>` reference would answer
    differently under the component reading — and no component of any ancestor
    exists while a local element is being mapped. One `Element.parent` walk is
    decidable at exactly the point the clause is charged.
  - **`p.target`, not the ancestor `<schema>`'s raw attribute.** The two genuinely
    diverge under `<override>`: the XML ancestor `<schema>` of a substituted
    declaration is the *overriding* document's. PRINCIPLES 16 settles it — the
    declaration takes the overridden document's schema-level defaults — and
    `localTargetNS` already mints the element's own namespace on that same
    footing, so reading the constraint on the other one would let the constraint
    and the mapping disagree about a single element. `foldDefaultAttributes` and
    `defaultOpenContentElem` take this reading too; `licensedNamespace` takes the
    other one only because src-resolve clause 4.1.1 asks for the *attribute* by
    name.
  - **Presence stays a distinct fact from an empty value.** `own || p.chameleon()`
    is the presence test, so a schema with no `targetNamespace` at all satisfies
    4.3's antecedent whatever the element wrote — pinned by a
    `targetNamespace=""` row that no other row would catch.
  - **Charging 4.1 is a sanctioned absorb, not creep.** The arbiter put it to
    `docs/WORKFLOW.md`'s scope rule and it answers no to all three questions: the
    grounding covers clause 4 entire including 4.1; no exported surface; and it
    cannot move a lane on its own, since both the old `e-props-correct` clause 1
    diagnostic and the new 4.1 one reject. A helper documented as "clause 4" that
    silently skipped 4.1 would be a comment asserting more than the code does. It
    is named in the commit body as the rule requires.
  - **The innermost `<restriction>`, on a reachability argument the arbiter
    checked rather than took.** `<restriction>` occurs only under
    `<complexContent>`, `<simpleContent>` or `<simpleType>`, each a child of a
    `<complexType>` or `<simpleType>`; reaching a second one while walking up
    from an `<element>` needs an intervening `<complexType>` (which ends the
    walk) or `<simpleType>` (which admits no `<element>` below it). At most one
    can stand between an element and its nearest `<complexType>`, so 4.3.2's
    existential reading and this innermost one pick the same element and the
    choice is unobservable.
  - **`baseMatchesAnyType` answers `false` for an absent or unbindable `base=`,
    and swallows nothing.** `produceComplexContent` charges the missing-`base`
    grammar fault and resolves `base=` at `produce_complex.go:934-946`, both
    BEFORE `complexContentType` descends into the content model that reaches the
    only caller here. `bindQName` rather than `resolveQName` is deliberate:
    re-asking the src-resolve clause 4 licensing question at a second position
    would double-charge it.
  - **Two stale doc comments corrected in the same commit**, the scope rule's own
    worked example. `produceLocalElement`'s doc asserted *"the ancestor axis is
    not walkable from an `*Element`"*, which the retained tree's parent link had
    already made false — the real reason `scopeParent` is a parameter is that the

    bullet 3 rather than creep past it, because `exitSeverity` ranks `0/1/2/3`
    at indices `0, 2, 3, 4` — strictly monotone in the number — so #720's
    aggregation is preserved for every pair it ever decided.

    has; an instance shown invalid is decided and one left undecided is not, so
    the weaker claim must not out-shout the stronger. Mason nominated the
    opposite reading for scrutiny and the arbiter took the landed one, noting

    through it would require making `Unevaluated` satisfy `error`; a consumer

  - **The spec has no "unevaluated" outcome at all, and the oracle said so

- Decisions made and why:
  - **A construct query, never a spelling of one.** `local[@attr[,attr…]]`
    positionally, matched on the resolved (namespace URI, local name) pair, with
    Clark notation (`{uri}local`) as the escape hatch for a non-XSD namespace. A
    braceless element name defaults to the XML Schema namespace; a braceless
    attribute name to no namespace, which is what an unprefixed attribute
    resolves to and how XSD's own vocabulary attributes are always written. The
    alternatives were a flag surface (`-ns`/`-elem`/`-attr`) with no consumer
    (STYLE T5) and a regex query — which **is** the defect: it cannot express
    "this construct, however it is spelled".
  - **`parser/xmltree` throughout, and the grounding left no other branch.** The
    Acceptance said "reuse it or state why it cannot be reused"; the arbiter ruled
    at grounding time that `NewReader`/`Token()`/`Name.Space()`/`Local()` export
    the whole loop with no internals, that all 93 UTF-16LE fixtures carry a BOM so
    **#361**'s markless-`encoding=` gap does not reach this corpus, and that
    *"cannot be reused"* was not an available answer — a hand-rolled decoder
    would have been a finding. Hit locations come from `StartElement.Loc()`, so
    they are lines in the **decoded** stream and the UTF-16 test pins line 5, not
    a byte offset.
  - **A malformed fixture is content, not failure.** The suite ships
    not-well-formed documents on purpose, so a parse fault is carried in
    `fixtureScan.Err` beside the hits found ahead of it, and **only an open/close
    failure** aborts the census at exit 2. The rejected alternative — call an
    unreadable file "not XML" — makes a permissions error look like a `.gif`,
    a silent fail-open.
  - **Every walked file is named, not counted away** (absorbed beyond the body,
    and **UPHELD** by the verdict on the merits, not merely on scope). The report
    lists both unread groups in full — 91 that broke off after at least one start
    tag, mostly `nistMeta/*.html`, and 57 holding no element at all, mostly
    `.dtd`/`.css`/`.json` — with the arithmetic `walked = read-to-the-end +
    partly + no-element` pinned as an invariant by
    `TestReportAccountsForEveryWalkedFile`. A census that counts what it could
    not read under-reports exactly as the greps did, which is this issue's own
    defect one layer down.
  - **`suiteindex` is named in CLAUDE.md's Surveys block and NOT in "Other
    commands"** (mason's judgment call, **UPHELD**). "Other commands" holds the

  `@` suffix names the ATTRIBUTES to report on each match and the example means
  "every `element`, printing its `targetNamespace` attribute". This pass ran

  reading and got **`0 occurrence(s)`** — a plausible-looking answer, not an
  error, since no attribute is named `http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema` and zero
  is the truthful count of the query as parsed. The second run

## 2026-09-06 — /retro (weekly, eighth) — **all six `blocked`-on-retro issues were found and ruled, which is the seventh retro's own fix working the first time it was tested — and the window's largest unowned cost was invisible to every queue: a backgrounded gate run does not survive the turn that started it, four costed sightings, `grep -rin foreground docs/ .claude/` returning nothing normative**; the process audit's four rulings (#1279 ONE PATTERN with the fix landed in CLAUDE.md's Writing section, #1220 the Acceptance ruling gains a TRUTH question, #925 takes the triplication fork into `STYLE D3`, #692 body prose never binds) are joined by three `ready` process issues discharged here rather than routed for a ninth week (#1087 absorbed, #1105 ruled option 3, #484 ruled option (d) at 33 days old); **the `## Acceptance` ruling is now stated ONCE in `/develop` step 3 and both agent files point at it**, discharging the advisory #1052's own verdict left standing; and `mason.md`'s handoff bar stops contradicting itself fourteen lines apart — the mutation is RUN, not imagined, which is four sightings' worth of rejects (#1048, #786, #472, #999) at one entry point

- Trigger: weekly `/retro`, Part 1 (chronicler) only; Part 2 is the steward's
  separate delegation and was running CONCURRENTLY in this checkout (Friction 1).

  (`docs/LOG/2026-08.md:42199`) and `origin/main` at **`5b0b805`**: **74
  landings** (3 of them parks — #732, #993, #846), **87** `post-land` stamps, 9
  `/backlog` passes, 1 `/retro`. Evidence: those entries' `Cost` and `Friction`

  and each regexed for the retro trigger; the `ready` `kind/process` queue; the
  open corpus paginated `p1..p3` at `per_page=100` (**271** open non-PR issues,
  page 3 short at 71 and re-requested per `docs/ROUTINES.md`); closed issues
  since 2026-08-23T14:00Z (**100**); `go tool lanestatus` on the committed tree.
- Cost — **1 chronicler.** No oracle, no warden, no mason, no arbiter: the diff
  holds no `.go` file, and every rule landed here is a ruling on a filed issue
  rather than an invention. Gate parts 1–3 run on the committed tree; part 1's
  `go test ./...` and part 4 are the orchestrator's before the PR, as at the
  seventh retro. Costs already ruled, one clause each: the uniform four-part

  `git log -S` over `mason.md` with one visible commit, so **no rule's landing

  `.md` files, no `.go` file, no expectations file, no `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` run (a
  chronicler cannot and did not run it). Lane figures below are read off
  `go tool lanestatus`, never recomputed.

- **THE FINDING — the most expensive unowned cost in the window is a container
  fact, and the reason nothing owned it is that no document uses the word.**
  Four costed sightings, none of them filed, all of them recorded as
  *"`/retro` material"*:
  - **#1047** (2026-08-27) — mason AND the arbiter, independently, each ended a
    turn believing a backgrounded multi-minute conformance run would still be
    going when they were next resumed. *"Twice in one session, from two
    different agents, is a pattern and not an anecdote."* That entry wrote the
    prescription verbatim: *"a delegating prompt that hands an agent the
    ~5-minute conformance gate must say to run it in the FOREGROUND and block
    on its actual exit code in the same turn."*
  - **#56** (2026-08-28) — a mason dispatch lost the same way to a restart.

    not a neighbour to it: a turn does not carry a live child process, so a
    backgrounded command is dead the moment the turn ends; run the gate and
    every other multi-minute command in the **foreground** and block on its real
    exit code in the same turn. **Deliberately NOT also written into
    `mason.md`, `arbiter.md` or `develop.md`'s delegation steps** — three copies
    of one instruction is the second encoding this retro is elsewhere ruling

## 2026-09-06 — #1282 — **`suiteindex`'s `hit` gains the one field that makes local-versus-top-level expressible — `Parent`, the resolved name of the element the match is a direct child of — and #1205's census, hand-written twice in one session at n=139 because no number of queries could ask it, is now reproduced from the tool alone at 139/133/6, figure for figure, by mason and independently by the arbiter**: **ARBITER ACCEPT round 1, zero findings**, `Ratchet: unchanged` measured AND structural, `surface: unchanged`, two files **+211/−3**. The whole change is a `[]xsd.QName` pushed on each start tag and popped on each end tag over the token stream `scanFixture` already walked, read **before** the push so the top of the stack is the parent — no second parse, no ancestor chain, no selector flag. The grounding's correction was absorbed by **refusing to act on it**: `xs:redefine` is not a spec-legal parent of a top-level `xs:element` (only `xs:schema` and `xs:override` are), and the package doc now says the tool reports the parent the document actually spells, *"never one corrected against the grammar"*.

- Cost — **1 oracle, 1 mason, 1 arbiter.** Zero repair rounds, zero rejects, no
  warden, no cartographer, one session start to finish. The dominant cost is
  again conformance on a diff that provably cannot reach it — mason's part 4,
  the arbiter's part 4, the ratchet run, plus each container's `conformance`
  leg inside `go test ./...` — and it is the gate kept uniform on **#881**'s
  ruling, cited rather than re-argued; `tools/suiteindex` being a `package
  main` nothing imports is the same fact as a doc-only diff wearing different
  clothes. The other ruled costs took a clause each: the submodule init per
  fresh container (**#659**), paid in both worktrees, and `go tool surface` run
  and reported as a surface check rather than a fifth gate step (**#304**).
- Decisions made and why:
  - **Absence is the zero `QName`, not a `HasParent bool`.** No legal name has
    an empty local part, so `{Space:"", Local:""}` cannot collide with a real
    parent, and a flag beside the name would be STYLE D3 state derivable from
    the name it sits next to. The report renders it `(none)`, which cannot
    collide either — parentheses are not NCName characters.
  - **The parent is read off the stack before the current element is pushed**,
    and every entry is the name `xmltree` resolved in **that element's own
    scope**. That disposes of the grounding's one named hazard (resolving the
    parent from the child's prefix) by construction: the tool never sees a
    prefix. `TestScanFixtureResolvesTheParentInItsOwnScope` makes it
    falsifiable with a child that rebinds the parent's prefix to `urn:decoy`.
  - **`sameName` folded onto the new `qnameOf` rather than left as a second
    copy** (STYLE T4), and the arbiter checked the fold was exact rather than
    plausible: `xsd.QName` is `struct { Space, Local string }` and nothing else
    (`xsd/qname.go:22`), so `want == qnameOf(got)` is identical to the two-field
    comparison it replaces. One helper added, one duplication removed.
  - **The `redefine` finding is honored by inaction, and written into the
    package doc instead.** The oracle ruled `xs:redefine`'s content model
    (`xmlschema11-1.md:4078`, the `xs:redefinable` restriction at `:4465-4477`)
    carries no `element` member, so an `xs:element` found under it sits in a
    document invalid against the schema for schemas — plausibly a deliberate
    invalid-schema fixture. A raw census must report it verbatim, so nothing
    reclassifies, drops or corrects, and the rule is stated where a later
    reader will hit it.
  - **The defensive `len(open) > 0` guard was removed and the invariant
    asserted in a comment**, on the reading that `xmltree` emits an end tag
    only for an element it holds open under a matching name. Mason named this
    the worst failure mode in the diff and asked for it to be attacked; the
    arbiter re-read `parser/xmltree/reader.go` and confirmed `endElement`
    (`:183-198`) returns an error and **no node** on all three failure shapes —
    empty stack, unbound prefix, name mismatch — pops only on success, and
    `handleReadErr` (`:95`) turns an unclosed element at EOF into an error
    rather than a synthesized end tag, so emitted `*StartElement`s and reader
    frames are one-to-one. It then went past reading: **five hand-built hostile
    fixtures, one per underflow shape**, no panic, exit 0, hits ahead of each
    fault retained, and the 42,265-file corpus run (91 partly-read fixtures)
    clean.
  - **The 139/133/6 pin is banked as a test**, `TestSuiteTopLevelCensusOfFinalAndAbstract`,
    corpus-pinned and skipping without the submodule (#659) alongside the
    existing `TestSuiteAcceptanceCases`, at ~4s. Mason flagged the question of
    whether it belongs in the suite at all; the Acceptance calls it the pin, so
    it is one.
  - **No selector flag.** The scope-out is honored exactly — no `-local`, no
    `-toplevel`, no filtering — and `docs/PLAN.md` and `docs/LOG` were left
    alone by mason as not its to write.
- Surprises:
  - **The pin's top-level set is wider than the corpus, and the test keeps the
    wider set anyway.** #1205's pin reads *"parent of `{XMLSchema}schema`,
    `{XMLSchema}redefine` or `{XMLSchema}override`"*, and this corpus
    contributes **zero** `redefine`- and zero `override`-parented hits: the 133
    is entirely `schema`. The test still asserts membership in all three,
    because the pin is stated that way and a fixture moving into `override`
    must not read as a regression — and because, per the grounding, one of the
    three is not even legal there.
  - **Both agents ran the same four mutations and the failure figures matched
    to the digit.** Deleting the pop fails `RecordsTheParent` and
    `ResolvesTheParentInItsOwnScope` and drives the suite pin to **`139 hits,
    44 top-level, 95 local`** in mason's run and the arbiter's alike; pushing

  - **The grounding re-read the Acceptance's own census sentence as an
    empirical grouping rather than a legality claim**, which is why its

## 2026-09-07 — #1246 — **`src-element` clause 3 stops being the ONE exception to walk-first, so every `src-*` charge in the parser is now behind its own s4s walk with no carve-out left to name: two `if` blocks moved past `checkS4SChildOrder` in `produceElement` and `produceLocalElement` — predicate, message and rule ID untouched — and `checkS4SChildOrder`'s DEFAULT paragraph and exception paragraph collapse into one order paragraph. The load-bearing half is that the choice was ruled ENGINEERING and labelled as such at every site: the oracle found the two checks operate on DISJOINT PREDICATE SPACES — an XSD content model has no vocabulary for "attribute X present implies child Y absent", which is why the SRC exists alongside the grammar at all — so neither check can ever preempt the other and run order decides only which `xsderr.Error` a doubly-invalid document surfaces. Option 1 and Option 2 are equally spec-consistent, and Option 2 was taken because the last three new `src-*` charges (#1243, #1270, #1275) each landed at the default**: **ACCEPTED round 1**, four non-blocking notes, `Ratchet: unchanged` predicted by census before implementation and then measured, `surface: unchanged`, five files **+230/−51**.

  nits and zero blockers. The dominant cost is conformance, two full part-4 runs
  plus each container's own conformance leg inside `go test ./...`, on a diff that
  cannot reach the harness at all — the doc-only/unreachable gate arm is **#881**,
  ruled and closed, and the gate stays uniform. The second largest is the
  arbiter's hand-probing: it built the binary and ran all four directive kinds
  (`import`, `override`, non-empty `redefine`, bare `import`) against it rather
  than reading mason's scope claims, plus five mutation tests, each killed.
  Documented costs, one clause each: the submodule init per fresh worktree
  (**#659**), paid in both containers; `go tool surface` run and reported as a
  surface check rather than a fifth gate step (**#304**); `docs/LOG/` empty at
  verdict time, which docs/WORKFLOW.md's step order requires (**#820**).
- Decisions made and why:
  - **Disposition (a) — report it — and the grounding forbids calling it a spec
    decision.** The oracle read `src-include` (§4.2.3), `src-import` (§4.2.6.2)
    and `src-override` (§4.2.5) and ruled BOTH dispositions the issue offered
    conformant: the spec makes the skip legal and says nothing about what a
    processor's operator interface owes for it, so this is a **pure CLI-contract
    choice** and the rationale is operator-facing, never clause-backed. What
    decided it is the filing evidence: the silence is total (exit 0, zero stderr)
    and the compiled schema is genuinely short of whatever the unread document
    declares.
  - **No rule ID, no exit-code move.** The line is a diagnosis of a legal
    outcome. `violationLine`'s form is `"<loc>: [<rule>] <message>"`, and a
    non-error printed in that shape reads as a spec charge to every consumer that
    greps for one.
  - **`UnfollowedNoLocation` is excluded, and the arbiter verified the narrowing
    rather than accepting it.** A bare `<xs:import>` names no document — §4.2.6.2
    makes it the spelling for *"references into this namespace are expected"* —
    so reporting it would charge a COMPLETE multi-document assembly with a
    shortfall. The arbiter probed a complete set by hand and confirmed the report
    would have misfired.
  - **`-q` does not suppress the line.** `-q`'s contract names `parse`'s summary,
    and the case this issue was filed from is a gate spelled `goxsd8 parse -q
    *.xsd` — a `-q` that swallowed the diagnosis would leave the silence exactly
    where the cliuser found it.
  - **The hint-augmented `compileSet` inside `validatorFor` was left untouched,
    deliberately.** What an unfollowed directive of a HINTED document owes the
    operator belongs to open **#1251**, and taking it here would have widened the
    landing into an issue that owns the question.
  - **A non-empty `<xs:redefine>` is out of scope because it was never silent.**
    `src-redefine` clause 1 is a MUST and already surfaces through the error
    `parser.ParseReport` returns (`parser/report.go:65-68` states this in the
    package's own words). Only the EMPTY form keeps `<include>`'s skip, and it is
    reported like one.
  - **All three contract copies moved together** — `cmd/goxsd8/doc.go`,
    `main.go`'s `usage` const and `README.md` — with `TestUsageCoversContract`
    gaining five pinned substrings.
- Surprises:
  - **The one narrowing that looked like under-reporting is the one a probe
    proved necessary.** Excluding `UnfollowedNoLocation` reads on the diff as a
    conservative omission; the arbiter's complete-set probe turned it into the
    condition for the feature being correct at all.
  - **`TestUsageCoversContract` couples less than mason's account claimed.** It
    asserts against the `usage` const alone, not against `doc.go`, so the two
    blocks agreeing today is a HAND result and not a mechanically proven one —
    the test's name reads as though it covered the contract wherever the contract
    is spelled.
- Friction — **nothing new. One sighting of an already-ruled class, cited rather
  than re-argued, and one class-of-cost that the process documents already
  place.** (a) The arbiter's nit 4 — `cmd/goxsd8/validate.go:490` holds a comment
  line at ~90 columns where its own paragraph wraps at ≤80, and `commentwrap`

## 2026-09-07 — #1007 with #1231, #1123, #1189, #1261 and #1290 — **six `cmd/goxsd8` contract defects land as ONE commit because all six edit the same three copies — `doc.go`, `main.go`'s `usage` const and `README.md` — and taking them apart rebases those three files six times. Five are prose; #1290 is not, and it REVERSES a documented, tested decision three days its senior: `goxsd8 parse order.xsd -q` stops printing the whole summary `-q` asked to suppress and then failing to open a file named `-q`, and `goxsd8 validate order.xml -schema order.xsd` stops answering "no schema given" to a command line that named one. The landing cost a reject round and the reject is the lesson: `cmd/goxsd8/doc.go:210` attached M9 to `codec` inside the ONE sentence #1123 exists to make accurate, while `docs/PLAN.md:898`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:523-524`, `codec/doc.go` and the module root `doc.go:15` all four already said M10 — a figure that four in-tree copies state correctly still did not survive from the grounding to the sentence**: **REJECTED round 1, ACCEPTED round 2 with zero findings**, `Ratchet: unchanged` run rather than inferred in BOTH rounds, `surface: unchanged`, eight files **+271/−62** over two commits.

- Decisions made and why:
  - **Six issues, one landing, and the reason is the three copies, not their
    size.** Every one of the six edits `cmd/goxsd8/doc.go`, `main.go`'s `usage`
    const and `README.md`'s CLI section, and #1189 and #1290 edit the same
    paragraph of `doc.go`'s `# Argument vocabulary` and the same two test
    files. Both groundings ended with the same landing note — take them in
    order or in one session — and `docs/PLAN.md` had already banded them as
    one.
  - **Spec: n/a for the whole bundle, ruled once and stated on all six
    threads.** The oracle read all five local specs and found none governs CLI
    exit codes, flag parsing, argument-order diagnostics or Go documentation
    accuracy. With no spec footing, the **arbiter** rules the `## Acceptance`
    and `## Surface` bullets instead — which is what the groundings say in
    their own opening lines, and what the two verdicts then held the
    implementation to.
  - **#1007 — `gen`'s exit codes are written honestly rather than withheld.**
    0 every pair generated, 1 a rejected schema, 2 an unreadable argument, an
    unwritable output directory or a `-schema` without its `-out`, worst
    outcome wins — modelled on `parse`'s and `validate`'s CURRENT wording, not
    on the issue table's stale quotes, and the sentence says outright that
    these are the codes `gen` answers with once M9 builds it and that until
    then every invocation exits 2. That is **#472**'s precedent for an unbuilt
    contract, verified against the binary.
  - **#1231 — the prose moved to the emitted verb, not the verb to the
    prose.** `doc.go` and `usage` said *"reserved but not yet built"* where
    `notImplementedFmt` prints *"not yet implemented"* and README already said
    "implemented", so the prose was the outlier: STYLE T6 fixes the house
    phrase and every other planned-surface `doc.go` in the module uses it.
    Moving the string would have moved `dispatchCases` and
    `TestBuiltBinaryMatrix` with it for no gain. **The pin is DERIVED, and that
    decision was made here rather than deferred to #398**:
    `TestUsageCoversContract` now builds the verb out of `notImplementedFmt`
    itself, so a drift on EITHER side fails. The arbiter ran it in both
    directions rather than reading the claim.
  - **#1123 — the closing claim is SCOPED, and the scope is wider than the
    issue asked.** *"every capability here is reachable through the public
    packages"* was false for three capabilities, not the two the body listed:
    the grounding added code generation to the issue's JSON/BER table, because
    `codegen/` and `codec/` hold only `doc.go` and README names `codegen`
    nowhere. The sentence now names what is reachable today and says
    `validate/jsonsrc` (M8), `codegen` (M9) with `codec` (M10) and
    `validate/bersrc` (M11) export nothing yet. `jsonsrc`, `bersrc`, `codegen`
    and `codec` are untouched — making the sentence true by shipping the
    packages is explicitly not this issue.
  - **#1189 — branch (b), DEVIATING from the grounding's leaning toward (a),
    and the arbiter said it would have ruled the same.** The remedy half —
    `leadingFlagFmt` must stop suggesting an invocation that itself fails — is
    owed under EITHER branch, and under (a) the only routes are to degrade
    `leadingFlagFmt` for every flag it is right about or to publish, in a
    contract the user reading stderr never sees, an exception to our own
    advice. `diagnose` gains a fifth answer instead: a valued help spelling
    earns `helpNotAFlagValue` in **both** pre-subcommand positions, which
    makes `doc.go`'s *"Both answers are usage errors naming the three
    spellings"* true as written for the first time. `wantsHelp` is untouched,
    the three bare tokens stay the whole help vocabulary, and `wantsHelp` and
    `valuedHelpFlag` read one `helpSpellings` encoding rather than a list each
    (STYLE D3/T4).
  - **#1261 — branch (a), the summary body is SPECIFIED and not disclaimed.**
    The stream is already committed for scripts (**#1066** put it on stdout for
    that reason) and pinned byte-for-byte by four `parse_test.go` goldens, so
    publishing it as unstable would have published a false uncertainty. The
    enumeration lands **verbatim in both `doc.go` and `usage`** — the
    grounding's ruling that the two are one copy in two renderings — with
    README pointing at `go doc`. **No second CODE encoding was added**: no
    labels slice, no test re-listing them; the existing goldens stay the pin,
    as the issue required.
  - **#1290 — arm B, bounded, and the reversal is STATED rather than deleted.**
    Each subcommand detects a flag-shaped token among its positionals before
    doing any work and answers with `flagAfterPositionalFmt`, placed at
    `parse.go:44` ahead of the compilation loop and `validate.go:118` ahead of
    both missing-argument diagnoses — which is what stops `validate` giving the
    omission answer to a line that named `-schema`. Arm A was declined on the
    grounding's cost ruling: Go's `flag` package does not intersperse, so it
    means reordering args before `Parse`, a `./-q` escape hatch anyway, and
    keeping the lone `-` a positional, while a `--` end-of-options marker is
    forbidden here because `doc.go:106-108` already decides `--` carries no
    such meaning and that is not this issue's to reopen. **The superseded
    sentence is quoted verbatim in the commit body and called false by
    design**, and `TestParseFlagAfterPositional` and
    `TestValidateFlagAfterPositional` are **INVERTED rather than deleted**,
    each recording in its own comment what it used to assert. The exact
    spelling `-` stays the standard-input instance argument; `./-q` is the
    escape hatch, stated in `doc.go` beside the existing `./-` precedent and in
    the diagnosis itself, and pinned by `TestParseFileNamedLikeAFlag`.
  - **The repair kept `codegen (M9) with codec (M10)` over the flat list the
    verdict also offered**, and the arbiter agreed on re-judgment: the sentence
    maps a package list onto a capability list whose later clause names exactly
    three capabilities, so `with` preserves the 3:3 correspondence a flat
    four-item list would break. Each package carries its own parenthetical,
    which was the whole defect.
  - **Absorbed and named, not creep**: README's *"one of four lines on stderr"*
    became five, `TestRunDispatch`'s and `dispatchCases`' comments count five

- Decisions made and why:
  - **Acceptance bullet 3 was FALSE as written, and the correction narrowed the
    design question before mason started.** It read *"Both a per-hit list and a
    tally answer the census above"* and offered dedup and a distinct-child-set
    tally as equal options. The census in bullet 2 has two halves, and the
    second — *"nor a second `simpleType`/`complexType` beside a first"* — is a
    **multiplicity** question, which dedup and a tally both discard by
    construction; a taker reading the menu as three equal options could have
    chosen one that made the preceding bullet unsatisfiable. The arbiter ruled
    it false at grounding and the cartographer re-stated the bullet in the body
    — full ordered list of direct children, repeats included, with
    **presentation** left open and left the implementer's — leaving Goal, Spec,
    the other five bullets, Surface, Notes and `## Depends on` byte-identical
    and the issue startable as it was.
  - **The unread signal is `hit.ChildrenUnclosed`, per match, and the
    parenthetical pointing at `report.Partial` was overruled at grounding.**
    `report.Partial` is per FILE and cannot carry the distinction; the
    counterexample is in the corpus and in the Notes' own 13-occurrence set.
    The mechanism is that whatever is still open when the stream ends never saw
    its end tag, so `markUnclosed` marks those hits — **every enclosing one,
    not just the innermost**.
  - **Presentation: INLINE on the match line**, between `parent=` and the
    queried attribute values, every name through `renderName`. `children=[]` is
    a match with no element child; a list whose last entry is `(unclosed)` is a
    prefix. The marker cannot be read as a name for the same reason `(none)`
    cannot — parentheses are not NCName characters. Chosen **over a companion
    section keyed by position**, because joining a hit to its children by
    position is exactly the hand reconciliation #1246 paid for and this issue
    retires, and a companion section reinstates it inside the tool's own
    output; and **over a rollup**, because a rollup is a projection *from*
    these lists and the reverse does not hold. Named in the commit body, which
    is what bullet 3 required and what the verdict checked.
  - **The stack carries the hit index, not a depth count.** `open` moves from
    `[]xsd.QName` to `[]openElem{Name, Hit}` with `Hit` an index into
    `fixtureScan.Hits` or `noHit`, so a start tag's direct parent is the top of
    the stack and nothing else, `recordChild` appends with no depth arithmetic,
    and **a match nested inside another match is not a special case** —
    `TestScanFixtureRecordsChildrenOfNestedMatches` pins a query matching at
    two depths. The hit is still appended at its **START** tag and only filled
    in afterwards, which is what keeps `Hits` in document order; appending at
    `EndElement` would have inverted nested matches, and
    `TestCensusIsDeterministic` and `TestReportAccountsForEveryWalkedFile` pass
    **unmodified** (the arbiter extracted both from each tree and diffed them:
    IDENTICAL).
  - **`renderParent` renamed `renderName`, one renderer for both sides.** The
    grounding flagged the rename as inside this issue and not a re-decision of
    #1297; taking it is what makes #1297's eventual fix reach parent and child
    from one site. Mason named the citation staleness it creates rather than
    leaving it to be discovered — see Next.
  - **No child SELECTOR**, honored exactly: the arbiter verified by extraction
    rather than by eye that `parseQuery`, `splitName` and `match` are
    **byte-identical** to `origin/main`. The dot-entry skip (#1266), `-h`
    (#1267), `latchWriter` (#1265) and #1297's namespace rendering are all
    untouched.

- Decisions made and why:
  - **A new unexported sibling at the site, not a child-position form of
    `rejectProhibitedAttrs`.** `rejectNamedGroupBodyOccurs(group, decl *Element)`
    lands in `parser/produce_complex.go` beside `rejectNamedGroupBody` and
    `repeatedCompositorChild` — the two guards that already own that child's
    identity and cardinality; this one owns its attributes. The alternative it
    beats is real and was argued rather than waved past: `rejectProhibitedAttrs`
    switches on the DECLARATION element's local name and hangs its production
    string on `topLevelGrammar(local)`, while the prohibition here is declared by
    a **different type per arm** — an inline anonymous `xs:complexType` for
    `<all>`, `xs:simpleExplicitGroup` for `<choice>`/`<sequence>` — at a position
    that function has no notion of. Threading a child through it means two
    grammar-lookup paths inside one switch and a `declForm` that no longer names
    a form. STYLE T4 picks the smaller change.
  - **No rule ID, and STYLE E2 makes that mandatory rather than merely
    permitted.** §3.7.3 reads *"None as such."* in full (`xmlschema11-1.md:2286`)
    and no `src-mgd` exists, so what binds is §5.1's first bullet (`:4296`)
    directly. E2's own carve-out names this class — a schema document simply not
    valid against the schema for schema documents, a prohibited attribute — and
    requires a plain error naming the item, its location and the Appendix A
    production. Every test row asserts `!errors.As(err, &xe)`, so the ABSENCE of
    the rule is pinned rather than left to inspection.
  - **The fault is PRESENCE, and that is what forecloses the obvious fix.**
    `use="prohibited"` excludes the attribute however it is spelled, so
    `minOccurs="1"` — the value `xs:occurs` declares as the default, a semantic
    no-op — is as much a fault as `maxOccurs="2"`. `allOccursGrammar`'s `{0,1}`
    enumeration admits both `maxOccurs="1"` and `minOccurs="0"`, so no widening
    of that check could ever have reached two of the six required rows. The
    issue body established this and it survived intact through grounding.
  - **Grammar declaration order, checked over a literal
    `[]string{"minOccurs", "maxOccurs"}`** (STYLE D2), so a body writing both is
    always reported at `minOccurs` whatever the document's order. **Mason added
    a seventh row beyond the issue body to make that falsifiable** — mgO019's
    exact shape, `maxOccurs="0" minOccurs="0"`, attributes in the opposite
    document order — and the arbiter ruled it the row that earns D2 its
    assertion.
  - **Call order: after `repeatedCompositorChild`, before `groupParticles`** —
    mason's first scrutiny request, CONFIRMED with no change and no pinning row.
    A body with two compositors has no single body to charge an attribute on, so
    the cardinality fault answers first, which is `rejectNamedGroupBody`'s own
    discipline; running ahead of the particles is `rejectProhibitedAttrs`'s, on
    the reasoning that the prohibited attribute is the mistake whatever the
    particles beneath it would also raise. The interaction is reachable only
    through a document already ill-formed twice over.
  - **The `grammar` default is total, and no caller-fault arm was added** —
    second scrutiny request, CONFIRMED. `rejectNamedGroupBodyOccurs` defaults to
    `xs:simpleExplicitGroup` and overrides for `all`; the arbiter read
    `compositorChild` and found its `switch` returns only on `"all"`,
    `"choice"`, `"sequence"`, so the domain at this call site is genuinely
    closed. The asymmetry with `rejectProhibitedRefAttrs`, which does carry such
    an arm, is not an inconsistency: that function switches on a name that can
    be anything and this one cannot, and an unreachable arm would encode a state
    the caller already forecloses.
  - **The local-compositor control was SUBSTITUTED, not satisfied, and the
    substitution is the load-bearing decision of the landing** — fourth
    scrutiny request, CONFIRMED as the stronger and the accurate pin. The
    Acceptance bullet asks for a control proving a local `<sequence
    maxOccurs="0">` inside a `<complexType>` "keeps its occurrence attributes",
    which reads as plain ACCEPT — and **plain ACCEPT was never true of that
    row**: it fails `p-props-correct` on the default `minOccurs="1"` greater than
    `maxOccurs="0"`, a value verdict one phase later, pre-existing this issue and
    unchanged by it. Satisfying the literal reading would have meant silently
    rewriting the row to `minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="0"` and pinning something
    weaker while claiming something stronger. What the bullet PROTECTS is that
    nothing here may reach a local position, and `TestProduceLocalCompositorKeepsOccurs`
    asserts exactly that for all six rows — the `use="prohibited"` prohibition is
    never what answers locally — plus, for the `maxOccurs="0"` row, the actual
    `p-props-correct` verdict. The arbiter's second mutation is what makes the
    ruling a measurement rather than a preference (see below).

The landing's load-bearing half is the CORRELATION — which of the operator's hints a wrapper-level `Unfollowed()` entry belongs to, the one thing the grounding scoped and deliberately did not decide — and mason's finding is that the grounding's OWN suggested answer is UNSOUND rather than merely imprecise: `Unfollowed()` records only the hints that FAILED, so one hint resolving ahead of one that does not shifts every ordinal mapping after it, and a three-directive case with the 1st and 3rd missing maps the surviving failure onto the WRONG document. - Decisions made and why:
  - **CORRELATION BY LAYOUT, not by ordinal and not by set difference** — the
    ruling the grounding left open, made by mason and verified by the arbiter
    from scratch. Every wrapper directive shares `At.URI == schemaSetLocation`
    and, before this, `At.Line == 1`, so the only handle a caller had was a byte
    column it cannot decode back to a document. One directive per line makes the
    line the index. **Ordinal correlation — the grounding's own candidate (c) —
    is unsound**: `Unfollowed()` holds only the hints that FAILED. **Set
    difference against `Documents()` is unsound for a different reason**: on a
    rejected assembly it cannot tell "did not resolve" from "never reached", the
    assembly having stopped early, and it conflates two hints naming one missing
    path into one entry.
  - **The position is read and never rendered.** `reportUnfollowedHints`
    (`cmd/goxsd8/validate.go:364`) prints `hinted[i].location` — the CLI's own
    `found []schemaDoc` — and cites neither `u.At` nor `schemaSetLocation`,
    because that location is this process's own synthesis and names no document
    the reader can open. `hintFault` already made exactly this choice for
    exactly this reason (STYLE E3), and the existing test forbidding any line
    that cites `schemaSetLocation` covers the new arm without amendment.
  - **`shortfallClause` (`parse.go:223`), a STYLE D3 consolidation absorbed on
    the way past.** The compiled/rejected two-wording logic mason itself
    introduced for #1312 hours earlier is lifted out of `reportUnfollowed` into
    one helper, reused byte-for-byte at the original call site, so both reporters
    of an unfollowed directive say it the same way and #1312's reasoning for the
    two wordings lives once.
  - **A hinted document's OWN nested unresolved directive stays unreported —
    mason's scoping upheld, mason's REASON corrected in the verdict.** The
    issue's Fact 2 defines the scope as the hint itself, and the arbiter ruled
    the decision right on that ground. But mason's account justified it as
    *"which `At.URI` cannot separate"*, and that is inverted: a nested hinted
    directive **is** separable by URI. What it actually lacks is separation from
    a `-schema` document's own nested directive, which `runValidate` already
    names — and reporting it here would double-report that one.
  - **One of the accept's three findings was applied on the branch, by the
    orchestrator's own pen** (`5515903`), under `docs/WORKFLOW.md`'s allowance
    for provably comment/`.md`-only edits. Both published contract copies —

- Surprises:
  - **The grounding's suggested design was not imprecise, it was WRONG, and the

## 2026-09-08 — #1227 — **landing precondition 3 stops iterating "mason commits" — a set nothing can compute, because on `wip/issue-<N>` every commit arrives through the orchestrating session's own git whichever agent wrote it, and #999's two carry identical authorship and identical trailers — and starts iterating IMPLEMENTATION commits, what `git log --no-merges --format='%h %s' origin/main..HEAD -- ':(top,exclude)docs/LOG/'` yields, each owed either a `MASON:` comment naming it or a named arm of the pen bound. The vacuity is the whole defect: #999's orchestrator-held branch cleared the precondition by having nothing to iterate, and that same branch is now the FAIL fixture. The load-bearing detail is the one mason asked to have scrutinized hardest and the arbiter nearly refuted — `(top)` is not decoration.   > The ·redefinition· applied to a reading is deliberately NOT part of it, so a

  `redefineSet.id` and `key()` are **deleted** with their sole reader, so the
  derivable identity the issue's Notes turned on is gone rather than re-encoded

  readings contribute": with two redefinitions the union is `S2 \ (E1 ∩ E2)`, and
  a plain reading excepts nothing, so a mixed plain+redefine document contributes

    `facetFixed`'s `(bool, error)`.** Presence is a RULE INPUT at three sites,
    not a fault: `produceSimpleContent`'s src-ct clause 1, the `ctElem`/`cc` pair
    driving `dcl.ctd.ctcc.common` clause 1.1-vs-1.2, and `foldDefaultAttributes`'s
    "only an ·actual value· of false opts out". The alternative — `(bool, error)`
    plus re-reading `el.Attr` at those three sites — spells the same attribute

    present**, matching `facetFixed`'s zero-value return. Documented on the
    function, and every one of the fourteen callers checks `err` before touching
    `present`, so it is unobservable. Raised by mason for scrutiny and ruled
    **advisory, not a finding** — symmetry over literal truthfulness, not
    required to change.

    `produceLocalAttribute`'s `inheritable` has one caller,
    `produceAttributeUse` (`produce_complex.go:3264`), which reads the same
    attribute off the same element at `:3248` and returns on the fault first —

    written out anyway because **a dropped error is the STYLE S3 fault whether or
    not a test can reach it**, and the test file states this rather than leaving
    a reviewer to rediscover it.

    existing `ruleDatatypeValid`, no new rule spelling. §4.1.4 applies the
    pre-lexical facet BEFORE lexical-space membership is tested, and states no
    fallback clause — so a padded `" 1 "` is the value `true` and an
    out-of-space `"yes"` must be charged, never defaulted to false.

- Decisions made and why:
  - **`formChoiceQualified(lexical, loc, attr) (bool, error)` as ONE encoding of
    `xs:formChoice`, read by both `localTargetNS` and the eager check.** The
    alternative it beats is a private two-value switch in each of those two
    places — which is the disease this issue is about, one level up. `attr` names
    the attribute in the message, since all three of `form`,
    `elementFormDefault` and `attributeFormDefault` are declared with that one
    type.
  - **The `*FormDefault` charge is eager and per document; `form=` and `use=`
    stay at their read sites.** Two different reasons, both written into
    `checkFormDefaults`' doc: a `*FormDefault` fault is a fault of the DOCUMENT,
    reachable or not, which is `checkDefaultOpenContent`'s content-independence
    argument verbatim and why the call sits beside it; every `form=` and `use=` a
    document writes, by contrast, is read by the declaration carrying it, which
    matches `processContentsOf` and `openContentModeOf`, the two keyword
    attributes in this package that already normalize AND charge.
  - **`localTargetNS` still reads `*FormDefault` through `collapseTrim` while
    charging nothing for it**, and that is load-bearing rather than belt-and-
    braces: the eager check ACCEPTS a padded-but-valid
    `elementFormDefault=" qualified "`, so a raw compare at the read site would
    then mint the declaration unqualified anyway. This is exactly the row the
    cartographer's item-2 restatement said the taker owed, and the arbiter pinned
    it by mutation — reverting to `fd == "qualified"` fails exactly the two
    padded `*FormDefault` rows.
  - **The error `formChoiceQualified` returns for `*FormDefault` is NOT routed
    back through `localTargetNS`** — the one design call the body did not settle.
    Routing it would add a genuinely unreachable error branch, since the eager
    check has already judged every document of the assembly; the read site is a
    plain compare with the invariant stated in its doc. The arbiter verified the
    invariant absolutely rather than taking it: `checkFormDefaults` is called at
    both and only both production entry points (`produce.go:148`,
    `parse.go:898`), `grep` finds exactly two `p.run()` sites each preceded by
    it, and in `compile` every document's check completes before any `p.run()`,
    so an on-demand build through `symbols.typeSource` cannot mint a local name
    off an unjudged `*FormDefault`.
  - **`boolAttr`'s landed shape, not `facetFixed`'s**, for the absent-versus-
    present-but-invalid split: both split the same two branches and `boolAttr` is
    the one in this file, landed by #456 the day before. Absent `use=` is the

  - **`collapseTrim`'s doc sentence naming the raw `use=`/`form=` compares is

## 2026-09-09 — #1167 — **`.claude/agents/mason.md`'s scope paragraph gains the one instruction it was missing: when your diff deletes a `GAP(` marker, sweep the WHOLE MODULE for the prose that deletion leaves stale, by two keys in the order that matters — the marker's owning identifier and its file name, then, over the prose around every hit, the OPERATION the marker recorded. The disposition is a document rule and NOT `gapaudit`'s third direction, and it turns on a measurement rather than a preference: a name/file join over #725's deleted marker returns **1 of the 6** stale sites that landing actually corrected, the other five paraphrasing the marker's recorded state and naming neither the marker, its function, nor its file — so PRINCIPLES 27 does not buy a tool at 20% precision against the population it is named for, and *"no, it stays the reviewer's grep"* is what the tree already had and is what produced sighting 2's round-1 REJECT. The landing's other half is what it cost to get here, and it is not the mason round: **this branch was held four times across 21 hours of 2026-09-09 and the first three holdings produced ZERO diff** — every one posted a correct `TAKEOVER:` naming the tip it found, pushed its heartbeat, and died before writing a line, so WORKFLOW's lease invariant worked exactly as written at every step and bought nothing, because it can record who took a branch and has no way to record that the previous taker reached nothing. The disposition was finally decided in a `TAKEOVER:` comment rather than by a fresh grounding, off a measurement a post-land pass for a DIFFERENT issue had posted seventeen hours earlier**: **ARBITER ACCEPT in round 1, zero blocking findings, zero repair rounds**, one advisory requiring no change to the tree and discharged by this entry, `Ratchet: unchanged` run in write mode rather than inferred, `surface: unchanged`, **one file `+6/−0`** in ONE content commit.

- Decisions made and why:
  - **The document rule beats `gapaudit`'s third direction on a measured
    precision, not on cost.** The THIRD SIGHTING comment's own join over
    `checkAttributeGroupRedefinitions` at #725's pre-landing base returned
    9 lines in 5 files — 5 candidates outside the defining file, of which
    **one** was the stale marker-pointing paragraph. The five sites that
    landing corrected which no name/file join returns say *"Phase A does
    NOT walk {attribute group definitions}"* and *"and finally — where
    Phase A stops — top-level attribute group definitions"*: the state,
    not the token. PRINCIPLES 27 reserves `kind/tooling` for repeated
    manual toil already measured, and the toil here is measured — but so
    is the tool's reach against it, and shipping the third arm would ship
    something that looks like a fix and reaches one site in six. The
    arbiter verified this against the tree (`git show 6b3759e --
    xsd/valueconstraintvalid.go`) rather than against the comment.
  - **`## Your standard`, integrated into the existing scope paragraph, is
    the host** — #1174's transferable half, *the host is the document whose
    own rule the miss breaks*. That paragraph already claims the class
    (*"stale comments and call sites your own diff breaks are cheaper
    absorbed than filed"*) and was missing only the instruction for finding
    this member of it. **Not `## Repair rounds`**, whose *"the claim you
    are correcting"* presupposes a verdict when this miss happens in
    mason's own sweep before any verdict exists — established on this
    thread on 2026-09-06, as the reason #925's ruling did not subsume this
    issue. **Not `## Before handoff`**, which is worktree, submodule, gate
    and mutation mechanics; a sweep rule filed there sits off the path the
    deleting mason walks, and *correct in the wrong place is
    undocumented* (#1279).
  - **Placed AFTER *"Do not go looking for adjacent work, and do not leave
    it behind when you find it"*, not before it**, so the sweep reads as an
    instance of that sentence's second half rather than as an exception to
    its first.
  - **The `since …` clause was kept and the arbiter ruled it load-bearing.**
    Mason offered it as the one clause an arbiter could cut to `+5/−0`.
    It is not a rule explaining why it is a good rule, which is what
    CLAUDE.md forbids; it is the 1-of-6 measurement in one clause, and
    without it *"search again by the operation"* reads as a restatement of
    *"grep the identifier and the file name"* and gets skipped — which is
    precisely the failure #725's sighting measured. On its one
    quantitative word, *"most"* holds at 5 of 9 across the two markers
    where anyone counted the split (3/3 name-joinable on #1115's marker,
    1/6 on #725's), and the imperative is unconditional either way.

    token anywhere; a sweep rule reads prose, and a test whose assertions
    encode a limitation has no prose to read. It stays unfiled at **n=1**,
    which is the ground on which no tool was built rather than a follow-up
    to build one.
  - **Sighting 1 (#414) is weaker evidence than the issue body's framing
    says, and a later reader should not count three instances of one
