## 2026-09-10 — #1361 — **the component build memos stop being keyed by expanded name and are keyed by the DECLARATION mapped: `symbols.builtComplex` and `symbols.builtGroups` go from `map[xsd.QName]…` to `map[*Element]…`, and a redefining `xs:group`/`xs:complexType` whose name is also contributed plainly stops being answered with the ORIGINAL. Name was only ever a proxy for the fact the memo encodes — "map one declaration at most once", because a second mapping re-registers the named `xs:unique`/`xs:key`/`xs:keyref` in its body — and §4.2.4 clause 4.1.2 makes the proxy routinely false: `redefinitions.excepts` is the INTERSECTION of a document's readings, so a document reached both plainly and through `xs:redefine` excepts nothing and original and redefinition both claim the name. Measured, `sch-props-correct` clause 2 stops citing `lib.xsd:2:3` as both of its two positions and names `r.xsd:3:5` as the offending one; the pairing handed `AddRedefiningModelGroup` becomes (redefinition, original), so `src-redefine` 6.2.2 is a two-term containment instead of V(R) ⊆ V(R); `src-expredef` 1.1/1.2 registers the redefinition rather than its own original. **The MIRROR case the body never named moved with it** — reverse the include order and the memo used to hand the REDEFINITION back for the redefined document's own dispatch, so BOTH positions read `r.xsd:3:5` and no original was registered at all — absorbed by the same one-line keying change rather than filed. **The load-bearing judgment is that the oracle's false-ACCEPT doubt was answered by a CALL-GRAPH trace and then re-derived independently by the arbiter, and it closes: a memo hit under `qn` implies a second registration under `qn`, and `indexByName` charges clause 2 inside `SchemaBuilder.finalize` before `Schema.resolve` ever reaches `checkModelGroupRedefinitions`, so clause 2 pre-empts 6.2.2 unconditionally and the severity is message quality, as filed.** That makes Acceptance bullet 3 **not constructible as written** — mason declared it undelivered and offered the finding to stand rather than write a test that pretends otherwise, and the arbiter ruled the bullet at fault, not the diff, then guarded the bullet's substance where 6.2.2 IS reachable by mutating `redefinedGroupRestricted` to build B := R and watching `TestParseRedefineGroupClause622` fail: **ARBITER REJECT round 1 on three findings, all of them stale prose of exactly the class mason's own 14-site sweep had already covered; ACCEPT round 2 with zero**, `Ratchet: unchanged` measured twice, `surface: unchanged` in both rounds, five files **+323/−115** over two commits plus one merge forward.

    floated.** A second memo or a `discardingComponents`-style bypass at
    `produceRedefinition`'s two call sites is a second encoding of "which
    component belongs to this build" (STYLE D3/T4), it leaves the identical
    latent substitution on every other route into the memos — the mirror case
    above, which the bypass would not have moved — and it can state a special
    case where re-keying states an invariant. No memo entry, no flag and no cycle
    check were added: the on-stack tri-state is the same tri-state read at a
    different key (PRINCIPLES 5/9 untouched).
  - **Element identity is a sound key ACROSS compositions, and the reason is
    `docKey`, not the memo.** A resolved location plus namespace plus override
    re-READS a document per key, so a chameleon-included or overridden document
    has a fresh `*Element` tree and its own entries — the same partition the old
    (name, composition) keying gave. The arbiter checked the other direction too:
    `overrideSet.replacement` matches on (kind, name) so a §F.2 substitute keeps
    the name, and `ov` cascades through `<include>`/`<override>` but never across
    `<import>`, so one `*Element` tree belongs to one `docKey` and one producer.

    one**, and mason flagged it as such rather than presenting it as neutral.
    Where the symbol table and the memo disagree about which of two colliding
    declarations a name addresses, the resolution now follows the table; both
    answers are arbitrary inside an assembly clause 2 rejects, and the memo's key
    set is a subset of the table's, so consulting the table first can turn no hit
    into a miss.

    constructible.** The literal bullet 2 — read `{derivation method}` off the

## 2026-09-10 — #1359 — **`TestCheckLandingRealHistory` stops reporting `ok` while running nothing: `requireFixtures` moves INSIDE each subtest and takes ONE pair, so an unreachable pair no longer takes down the two whose fixtures are in the object store, and there is no skip path left anywhere in the package — an unusable pair is fetched from `origin` by full 40-character hash and, failing that, FAILS. Its bar moves from presence to USABILITY (both commits resolve AND `merge-base --is-ancestor base head` holds), because the `--depth=1` trap mason measured makes those two different questions: a depth-1 fetch delivers commits without parent links, so the pair reads present and then fails landing precondition 2 as a STALE BASE — a second misdiagnosis planted where this issue is removing the first. The fetch is therefore undepthed, under a 60s `exec.CommandContext` timeout with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, and the hardcoded "shallow clone? run: git fetch --unshallow" string is replaced by `recoveryHint`, which measures `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` AT FAILURE TIME and prints the fetch's own exit status and stderr under it. **The load-bearing decision is the one the issue offered as the safe half of arm (c) and mason REFUTED by measurement: a skip kept for a "genuinely shallow clone the tool can detect" would fire in the very container that motivated this issue** — this container reads `--is-shallow-repository` → `true` and the by-hash fetch works here anyway — **so that hatch would exit 0 and leave the false coverage exactly where it was. Shallowness is not what makes a fixture unavailable, so it is not a valid excuse for a skip.** The recovered coverage is real and both agents proved it the same way rather than asserting it: degrade `checkLogEntry` to the non-empty-diff check `main.go:5-12` says it must not be, and **exactly one test in the package catches it — the #813 real-history subtest that was being skipped**: **ARBITER ACCEPT round 1, zero blocking findings, zero repair rounds**, five non-blocking findings routed to the post-land pass un-actioned, `Ratchet: unchanged` run in write mode rather than inferred, `surface: unchanged`, **one file `+104/−19`** in ONE commit.

    verdict, it declined to run at all"* — and `go test` has no exit 2, so a
    declined run has two honest encodings, fail or be invisible, and invisible is
    the defect. The escape hatch the issue paired with (c) was dropped on the
    measurement above rather than on preference. Neither agent cited a STYLE or
    PRINCIPLES rule for it, on the grounding's explicit instruction: both
    documents were grepped and say nothing about `t.Skip`, network-in-tests or
    false coverage, so this is judgment inside the issue and fabricating a letter
    ID would have been the finding.
  - **(b) — a pushed `refs/fixtures/*` ref — rejected on a fact, not on cost.** A
    default clone's refspec is `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`, so such a
    ref reaches a fresh container only if something fetches it explicitly; (b)
    therefore still needs a fetch at test time, which collapses it into (a) plus
    a remote-side push mason is worktree-isolated from performing. Landing a fix
    whose correctness waits on a push nobody has made was declined outright.
    Vendored DIFFS stay out for the reason `main_test.go`'s own header gives
    (#304, #735): the fixtures are real commits so the test runs the identical
    git invocation the landing would have run.
  - **No local `refs/fixtures/landcheck/<sha>` cache.** The measured repeat cost
    is 0.12s with zero network — the objects persist, and a `git gc` prune
    self-heals by re-fetching — so a ref would buy nothing the object store does
    not already give, at the price of a test writing into a developer's ref
    namespace.
  - **Undepthed fetch, in both directions.** `--depth=1` plants the stale-base
    misdiagnosis above; any `--depth` on a COMPLETE clone newly truncates history
    the developer had. Only the undepthed form is safe in both, and it does not
    silently unshallow the caller (measured: `--is-shallow-repository` still
    `true`, `rev-list --count HEAD` still 5, after fetching both hashes in 3.3s).
- Surprises:

    mental model that exactly #813's pair is the problem.
  - **`git merge-base --is-ancestor` SHORT-CIRCUITS, and the arbiter reached the
    state where that matters (N1).** It exits 0 the moment base is reachable from
    head, printing `error: Could not read <oid>` for an object it never needed,
    while `git diff base...head` — the command actually under test — does need it
    and dies `128 no merge base`. The guard then passes, no fetch is attempted,
    and the failure is a bare `exit status 128` with no pair named and no
    `recoveryHint`: this issue's own misdiagnosis shape, moved one step
    downstream and NOT self-healing. Non-blocking because reaching it requires an
    `origin` serving truncated history — the arbiter produced it only by pointing
    `origin` at a shallow local repo — and against GitHub all three
    `git diff base...head -- docs/LOG/` invocations exit 0 in this shallow
    container. The cheap fix is on the thread: probe with `gitDiffLog` itself, or
    with plain `git merge-base`, which does not short-circuit.
  - **Both agents ran the same mutation independently and got the same one-line
    answer**, which is what turns "recovers coverage" from a claim into a
    measurement: degrade precondition 1 to `if len(added) > 0 { return 0 }` and
    only the #813 subtest fails. `TestIssueTokenPattern` passes throughout — it
    exercises the pattern, not its use — so that regression was uncoverable
    before this change and the gate read `ok`.
